body_ar:
حكم الوضوء قبل دخول الوقت هل يجزئ الوضوء للصلاة قبل دخول الوقت؟

أنه أفضل، فبقاء الإنسان على طهارة دائما إن استطاع من فضائل الأعمال، وهو سبب سبق بلال إلى الجنة، فقد كان كلما أحدث توضأ وكلما توضأ صلى ركعتين.

------------------------------------------------------

حكم من لا يستطيع تحريك يمينه امرأة مصابة بمرض عصبي لا تستطيع الوقوف بنفسها ولا تتصرف بيمينها هل يسقط عنها الوضوء إذا أرادت الصلاة؟

ما دامت تجد من يساعدها على الوضوء ويقوم بغسل أعضاء الوضوء فلا يسقط عنها الوضوء، بل ربما يكون من علاجها وسببا لشفائها إن شاء الله، وإذا لم تجد من يساعدها في ذلك فلا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها.

حكم تطهير الثوب عند الغسال

من يضع ملابسه عند الغسال إذا كان فيها نجس ولم يخبره به هل تطهر بذلك أم لا؟

أن طهارة الخبث لا تشترط لها النية فليست مثل طهارة الحدث، والقاعدة الفقهية أن كل تعبد في الغير لا يحتاج إلى النية، كل تعبد في الغير لا يحتاج إلى النية، فغسل الميت لا يحتاج إلى نية، وتطهير الثوب أو المكان لا يحتاج إلى النية، لكن لا بد أن يعلم أن الغسال يضع الثوب في ماء قراح ليس متغيرا، لأن جمهور أهل العلم أن الماء المطهر الطهور الذي وصفه الله بذلك في كتابه في قوله وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا، وفي قوله في ماء المطر ليطهركم به ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان فإنما يطهر الماء المطلق الذي لم يتغير شيء من أوصافه الثلاثة، وقد ذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أن كل مائع قلاع يزيل أثر النجاسة تطهر به ويذهب به حكمها، وهذا القول ذهب إليه بعض المالكية ومنهم القرافي رحمه الله، وهو مذهب الحنفية، لكن الأول أحوط وأنقى، فعلى الإنسان أن يتعهد الطهارة في هذا المجال.

-----------------------------------------------------

رفع الحدث بالتيمم أنا متزوج وكثيرا ما أصلي بالجنابة خاصة في فصل الشتاء وذلك لأني مصاب بحساسية من البرد ولذلك لا أستطيع أن أغتسل فما الحكم؟

أن العاجز عن الغسل يلزمه التيمم لقول الله تعالى: {وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه} فلذلك يقوم التيمم مقام الغسل والوضوء في حق العاجز عن استعمال الماء وفاقد الماء، فالمريض الذي لا يستطيع استعمال الماء حكمه التيمم فيفعله طاعة لله وامتثالا لأمره ويستبيح به ما منع عليه.
body_en:
The ruling on performing ablution before the time of the prayer has come in. Does ablution for the prayer suffice before the time has come in?

It is better. A person's remaining always in a state of ritual purity, if he is able to, is among the meritorious deeds; and it was the cause of Bilal's going ahead into the Garden, for whenever he broke his ablution he performed ablution, and whenever he performed ablution he prayed two units of prayer.

------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on one who cannot move her right hand. A woman afflicted with a nerve disease who cannot stand by herself and cannot use her right hand — is ablution waived for her if she wishes to pray?

So long as she finds someone to help her with the ablution and to wash the limbs of ablution for her, ablution is not waived for her; rather it may be part of her treatment and a cause of her cure, God willing. And if she does not find anyone to help her in that, then God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.

The ruling on the purifying of a garment at the launderer's.

Someone who leaves his clothes with the launderer when there is something impure on them and does not tell him of it — do they become pure by that, or not?

Purification from filth (ṭahārat al-khabath) does not have intention as a condition for it; it is not like purification from the state of ritual impurity (ṭahārat al-ḥadath). The legal maxim is that every act of devotion performed upon something other than oneself does not require intention — every act of devotion performed upon something other than oneself does not require intention. So the washing of the dead does not require intention, and the purifying of a garment or of a place does not require intention. But he must be sure that the launderer puts the garment in pure unmixed water that has not been altered. For the position of the majority of the people of knowledge is that the purifying and purificatory water, which God described as such in His Book in His words 'And We sent down from the sky pure water', and in His words about rainwater 'that He might purify you by it and remove from you the defilement of Satan', is only unrestricted water (al-māʾ al-muṭlaq), none of whose three qualities has been altered. Some of the people of knowledge held that every detergent liquid that removes the trace of the impurity purifies by it and by it the impurity's ruling goes away. This position was held by some of the Malikis, among them al-Qarafi, God have mercy on him, and it is the position of the Hanafis. But the first is more cautious and cleaner, so a person should take care over purity in this domain.

-----------------------------------------------------

Lifting the state of ritual impurity by dry ablution. I am married, and I often pray in a state of major ritual impurity (janābah), especially in the winter season, because I suffer from an allergy to cold and therefore cannot perform the full washing. What is the ruling?

One who is unable to perform the full washing is obliged to perform dry ablution (tayammum), on account of the words of God, exalted: {And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you has come from the privy, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take to clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:6). Therefore dry ablution stands in the place of the full washing and of ablution in the case of one unable to use water and of one who lacks water. The sick person who cannot use water — his ruling is dry ablution; he does it in obedience to God and in compliance with His command, and by it he makes lawful for himself what had been prevented to him.

flags.arabic: أنا متزوج وكثيرا ما أصلي بالجنابة … فما الحكم؟
flags.context: the fourth question, set against the answer given
options: render faithfully and mark that the past prayers are not ruled on
present the answer as covering the prayers already performed
supply a ruling on making them up
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY — THE PRACTICAL HALF OF THE QUESTION IS NOT ANSWERED. The questioner states that he has repeatedly prayed in a state of major ritual impurity, without purification of any kind. The Sheikh answers what he should do from now on — dry ablution — and says nothing whatever about the prayers already performed, whether they were valid or whether they must be made up. That is the question the man is really asking, and it is left unanswered. Nothing has been supplied. Compare record 600 of this slice, which does treat making up past prayers but under a different framing; the two must not be read into each other.

flags.context: the first two sections of this record are served again, alone, as article 589
options: flag the duplication and treat this record as the fuller one
suppress 589 in favour of this record
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT — DUPLICATE, AND THIS IS THE FULLER RECORD OF THE PAIR. The first two fatwas here appear verbatim as the whole of article 589 of this slice, which also carries a .docx download that this record does not. So 581 has four fatwas complete on the page, and 589 has the first two and a download link. Same CMS duplication pattern as 396/397/400, 409/410, 419/420 and 561/563. Not deduplicated unilaterally; the Sheikh's office should decide which is canonical, but this record carries more text.

flags.arabic: كل تعبد في الغير لا يحتاج إلى النية
flags.context: the legal maxim, stated twice in succession
options: every act of devotion performed upon something other than oneself does not require intention
every act of worship directed at another does not require intention
any prescribed act performed on behalf of another needs no intention
flags.note: The maxim is compressed and its Arabic is not transparent; the Sheikh's own two examples — washing a corpse, and purifying a garment or a place — show that al-ghayr means the object acted upon, not a person on whose behalf one acts, which rules out option 3. The maxim is not in the glossary's list of legal maxims and should be added. Note that the repetition is in the source and is the Sheikh's own spoken emphasis; it has been kept rather than tidied away.

flags.arabic: وقد ذهب بعض أهل العلم … وهذا القول ذهب إليه بعض المالكية ومنهم القرافي … وهو مذهب الحنفية، لكن الأول أحوط وأنقى
flags.context: the two positions on what liquids purify, and the Sheikh's preference
options: keep both positions attributed and render the preference as a preference, not a ruling
present the majority position as the ruling and the other as rejected
present the Sheikh as holding the Maliki/Hanafi position
flags.note: IMPORTANT FOR ATTRIBUTION AND FOR RULING STRENGTH. The Sheikh reports the majority position; then reports a second position held by some Malikis, naming al-Qarafi, and by the Hanafis; and then says only that 'the first is more cautious and cleaner'. aḥwaṭ is the language of precaution, not of ruling: he does not say the second position is wrong, invalid or impermissible, and he is departing here from a position held within his own school. None of that may be hardened in English, and both attributions must stay unmistakable.

flags.context: the distinction on which the third fatwa rests
options: purification from filth / purification from the state of ritual impurity
removal of impurity / removal of ritual impurity
cleansing of substance / cleansing of state
flags.note: The glossary fixes ḥadath as 'state of ritual impurity' and najāsah as 'substantive impurity', noting that the two are distinct — a state versus a substance. khabath is used here where the glossary has najāsah, and the Sheikh switches to najāsah himself a few lines later. The English keeps his two words distinct so the reader can see the switch. khabath is not in the glossary and should be added alongside najāsah.

flags.arabic: وإذا لم تجد من يساعدها في ذلك فلا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
flags.context: the close of the second fatwa
options: render faithfully and mark that the alternative is never named
read it as waiving the prayer
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY — STYLE GUIDE §10. The Sheikh answers the case where help is available and then, for the case where it is not, quotes a verse and stops, without saying what the woman actually does. Note the irony that the fourth fatwa in this same record gives exactly the answer the second one withholds — dry ablution for one unable to use water — but he does not make that connection here and it has not been made for him. The wording of the verse is Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:286 and the source gives it unmarked, running on from his own sentence.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

COMPOUND RECORD. Four separate fatwas are served under one general title. The first, second and fourth are divided by rules of hyphens in the source; the third is separated only by a line break, so the boundary before it is weaker than the others. The site should present them as four distinct items.
Each fatwa opens with a sub-heading in the source which then runs into the question; all have been kept as the source has them.

The two Qur'anic citations in the third fatwa are given unmarked, running on from the Sheikh's own sentence, so the reader cannot see where his words end and scripture begins; preserved as the source has it. The wordings match Sūrat al-Furqān 25:48 and Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:11.

The Qur'anic citation in the fourth fatwa is given in curly braces in the source without a reference; the reference has been supplied. The wording with the final minhu matches Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:6 rather than the parallel at Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:43.

'Pure unmixed water' renders māʾ qarāḥ, and 'unrestricted water' renders al-māʾ al-muṭlaq, the technical category; the glossary's entry for muṭlaq ('unqualified') is the same word in its usul sense, and a reviewer may wish to record the fiqh sense separately.
'The three qualities' are the colour, taste and smell of the water; the Sheikh does not name them and they have not been supplied.
